patch_description:
The previous approach used a 160-member differential-evolution population for 360 generations, optimized a lower-tail surrogate over freely moving square points, and then applied 2,200 single-point local moves to six finalists. Its main weakness is that many global-search candidates have a hull substantially smaller than the unit square, so raw triangle-area optimization does not consistently optimize the normalized evaluation metric.

This version fixes the four unit-square corners, making the convex hull area exactly one for every candidate. It uses a larger 192-member population, 460 current-to-elite differential-evolution generations, a stronger early mutation range (0.82 to 0.48), and a 20-triangle lower-tail surrogate. The polish phase uses batches of active-constraint-targeted proposals: points participating in the smallest 14 triangles are selected preferentially, with occasional two-point mutations. This directs local evaluations toward the triangles controlling the true minimum area while retaining deterministic seeded behavior.
